title: Study Links PTSD in WTC Responders to Signs of Accelerated Biological Aging
detail: Researchers affiliated with Stony Brook University's WTC Health and Wellness Program published findings showing that World Trade Center responders with post-traumatic stress disorder exhibit biological markers of faster aging and increased frailty roughly 25 years after the attacks, compared to responders without PTSD. The study links PTSD to changes in cellular and inflammatory processes that may help explain the elevated rates of chronic disease — including cardiovascular and metabolic conditions — documented among Ground Zero responders in long-term WTC Health Program surveillance. Researchers say the findings support continued mental health screening and treatment as part of the program's long-term monitoring, since psychological trauma appears to compound the physical toll of toxic dust exposure.

media.caption: Research on WTC responders finds PTSD linked to accelerated biological aging, June 2026
